column1: # LOG-PORT-ONLY.tsv - port log emissions with NO reference counterpart, subtracted from the port count.
# Read .port/tools/gates/check_log_reconcile.py first; this file is only data.
# WHY (NEW-FINDINGS.md N81). G-LOGFILE counts a reference file's live `log.*` sites against the
# live emissions of the Rust files declared to port it, with deficit = max(0, reference - port).
# A port emission with no reference counterpart is counted anyway, and because a surplus is clamped
# it is invisible: it credits its file with one site that is not there and so MASKS the next real
# loss in that file. Measured: `src/terminal/PageList.zig` read 23 reference / 24 port because of the
# port-only R13 degrade warning, and deleting the genuinely ported `PageList.zig:775` site left the
# gate GREEN. Every row here is subtracted from the port count of EVERY portmap arm that contains its
# port file, before any comparison. A declaration can only make the count stricter.
# oracle_file   the reference file this emission would otherwise be credited to. Its portmap arms
#               MUST contain port_file, or the row is RED.
# port_file     the Rust file holding the emission.
# function      the innermost enclosing Rust `fn` of the emission, optionally `name#k` = the k-th
#               matching emission inside that fn in file order (only for textually identical copies,
#               e.g. a `#[cfg]` twin). Keyed on the call site, never on a line number: lines drift.
# match         a substring of the emission's call text (from the macro/fn name to its closing
#               delimiter, whitespace collapsed; comments excluded, string contents included).
# kind          one of: r13-handling, rust-only-path, abi-guard, instrumentation, expansion,
#               open-finding. `expansion` is an EXTRA static copy of ONE reference site (an
#               unrolled inline-for, a cfg/feature twin, one reference call split across two arms);
#               the first copy stays counted as that site's counterpart and only the extras are
#               declared. `open-finding` is a port-only emission that is itself an open
#               NEW-FINDINGS defect: delete the row in the commit that fixes it.
# reason        mandatory. A declaration with no reason is RED.
# Every row must resolve to EXACTLY ONE live production emission: none is RED (stale), more than one
# is RED (ambiguous), two rows selecting one emission is RED. The row count is capped, two-way:
# more rows than the budget is RED, fewer is RED (tighten it in the commit that removed a row). A
# missing directive BLOCKS. Messages containing a TAB or newline are written `\t` / `\n`.
